findings.note: The OM-16 finding at storage/__init__.py:14, which asks for new tenancy and audit namespaces, is not borne out by the source. The evidence lists passing tenancy to storage, with no org_id on entities, as correct, so this is advice the guideline does not appear to support.
The OM-03 finding at bin.py:9, which requires a MANAGER_OWNED_FIELDS tuple on every entity, rests on a symbol that appears nowhere in the checkout and cannot be verified against the source.
The OM-05 finding at stock_movement.py:6 restates the planted OM-06 defect at the same line under a second lens, which double-counts one issue.
Findings name lens, file, line, and fix, but none quotes the rule it rests on. None separates what the guideline requires from reviewer preference.

strengths: All eight planted defects are reported with the correct lens id at the exact file and line: OM-04, OM-17, OM-03, OM-13, OM-06, OM-12, OM-10 and OM-15.
No item on the clean list is flagged; the review even contrasts update_warehouse with delete_warehouse's correct model_validate rebuild.
Every finding gives a concrete, correct fix, such as new_id() for uuid4() and a now argument for is_stale.
The review reports the checker failure honestly and reads the code instead of staging or editing anything.
verdict.rationale: Recall is complete: every planted finding is hit at the right file, line and lens. Precision loses points for the unsupported OM-16 call for tenancy and audit namespaces, and for an unverifiable MANAGER_OWNED_FIELDS claim, plus a minor duplicate under OM-05. Form is good on lens, location and fix but omits rule quotes and the required-versus-preferred split.
